history.summary: A 1938-built, 99-year leasehold pre-war walk-up in the Tiong Bahru conservation belt (D03), asking $1.299M. Charming heritage location but the lowest score in the batch (156) reflects a near-90-year-old leasehold with severe lease-decay, financing and resale constraints.
history.rating_rationale: Built 1938 on a 99-year lease — remaining lease is critically short, triggering CPF-usage and bank-financing restrictions that gut the buyer pool. Tiong Bahru heritage charm supports own-stay demand but not investment math: lease decay works against you every year of a 5-7yr hold, and no URA series confirms any appreciation. Score 156 is the floor of the batch for good reason.

Lease decay actively erodes value over the hold
